subject: Issue with database connections being dropped

messages.author: af7187bd1c3ecb67
messages.subject: Issue with database connections being dropped
parts:
Hi, 

I'm running into an issue that I can't seem to resolve. I'm using dplyr in a Shiny app. When I leave the app open for a moderately long time but I'm not actually interacting with the app, dplyr disconnects the connection to my Postgres database. This probably happens when dplyr is garbage collecting. I've tried to modify src_postgres() in such a way that disco = db_disconnector(con, "postgres") is taken out of the call to src_sql so that I can handle the disconnections myself. Unfortunately this doesn't help. 

The other thing I've tried was that instead of feeding my tbl() definitions a call to an object created by src_postgres(), I fed them with a custom function that checks whether the connection to the database is still open. Although the function itself works fine, the objects created by tbl() don't reuse the function but inherit the database connection settings when the function is initially run. This means that when for example performing a filter on a tbl() object, the connection to the database is not checked but I'm always using the connection from src_postgres that was initially run when I created the tbl object. This means that when dplyr disconnection my initial connection to postgres, refreshing the connection doesn't make sense. 

I would really appreciate some guidance on how to elegantly solve this. The only option I see for now is to create functions of all my tbl definitions to check for open connection but this seems like hitting a needle with a hammer. 

An example of what I'm using now based on https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/0VjQc2a6z3M/discussion: 


dbConnection() <- function() {
  
  if (!exists('connection')) {
    connection <<- src_postgres(dbname = "postgres", 
                              host = postgres,
                              port = 5432, user = "postgres", password = "password")
  } else if (class(try(RPostgreSQL::dbGetQuery(connection$con, "SELECT 1 from table"))) == "try-error") {
    RPostgreSQL::dbDisconnect(connection$con)
    connection <<- src_postgres(dbname = "postgres", 
                              host = postgres,
                              port = 5432, user = "postgres", password = "password")
  }
  
  return(connection)
}

my_tbl <- tbl(dbConnection(), "my_table")



Many thanks for any help,

Niels

Hi Hadly,

Actually I'm pretty sure that the issue arises because my database connection is timing out. I was just wondering whether anyone has dealt with this issue when this happens. What I've done now is set the timeout of my database to be larger than the Shiny app but I'm sometimes still running into issues when my Shiny app doesn't use the database connections. 

Thanks,

Niels
